abstract: Extracellular protein interactions mediated by cell surface receptors are fundamental to intercellular communication and immune regulation. Identifying novel ligand-receptor interactions helps uncover previously unknown signalling pathways and improves understanding of immune mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a methodology aimed at facilitating the detection of cell-surface binding or proximity through flow cytometry. We demonstrate the efficacy of employing DTSSP (3,3'-dithiobis sulfosuccinimidylpropionate) crosslinking in conjunction with high-dimensional flow cytometry to achieve enhanced detection of cell-surface association while preserving the integrity of single-cell immune profiling. This strategy provides a versatile methodological framework for studying cell-surface interactions across heterogeneous immune cell populations.
